text: CVS Health Corporation, a Delaware corporation with its principal executive offices at One CVS Drive, Woonsocket, Rhode Island 02895, filed an annual report on Form 10-K pursuant to Section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. The registrant’s Commission file number is 001-01011, and its IRS Employer Identification Number is 05-0494040. The Company’s common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol CVS. As of June 30, 2022, the aggregate market value of the registrant’s common stock held by non-affiliates was approximately $121,258,020,752, based on the closing price of the stock on the New York Stock Exchange, with executive officers and directors considered affiliates for this calculation. As of February 1, 2023, the Company had 1,284,111,667 shares of common stock outstanding. The Company’s business is organized into four reportable segments: Health Care Benefits, Pharmacy Services, Retail/LTC, and Corporate/Other. The Health Care Benefits segment serves an estimated 35 million people as of December 31, 2022, offering a broad range of traditional, voluntary, and consumer-directed health insurance products and related services, including medical, pharmacy, dental, and behavioral health plans, medical management capabilities, Medicare Advantage and Medicare Supplement plans, standalone Medicare Part D prescription drug plans (PDPs), Medicaid health care management services, and health information technology (HIT) products and services. Prior to July 31, 2020, the segment also provided workers’ compensation administrative services through its Coventry Health Care Workers’ Compensation business, which was sold on that date. The segment’s customers include employer groups, individuals, college students, part-time and hourly workers, health plans, health care providers, governmental units, government-sponsored plans, labor groups, and expatriates. The Company refers to insurance products where it assumes all or a majority of the risk for medical and dental care costs as “Insured” and administrative services contract products where the plan sponsor assumes such risk as “ASC.” The Health Care Benefits segment offers commercial medical products such as point-of-service (POS), preferred provider organization (PPO), health maintenance organization (HMO), and indemnity benefit (Indemnity) plans, including health savings accounts (HSAs) and consumer-directed health plans that combine traditional POS or PPO and/or dental coverage with an accumulating benefit account, which may be funded by the plan sponsor or member. In 2021, the Company launched Aetna Virtual Primary Care™, enabling eligible members to access remote health services alongside in-person visits at MinuteClinic® locations. The segment also offers medical stop loss insurance for certain employers who self-insure, under which the Company assumes risk for large individual claims or aggregate losses above a pre-set annual threshold. The Company’s operations were significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, during which it offered diagnostic testing at more than 4,700 CVS pharmacy locations, community-based testing sites in underserved areas, and through its Return ReadySM solution as of December 31, 2022. It began selling over-the-counter (OTC) test kits in retail locations and online in 2021. The Company began administering COVID-19 vaccinations in long-term care facilities and certain retail pharmacies in December 2020 and February 2021, respectively, and started administering boosters and pediatric vaccines in the fourth quarter of 2021. As of December 31, 2022, the Company offered vaccinations at more than 9,000 CVS pharmacy locations. During the year ended December 31, 2022, the Company administered more than 15 million COVID-19 tests, nearly 28 million vaccines, and sold over 63 million OTC test kits. The Company expects to continue playing a significant role in testing and vaccine administration, maintaining a commitment to equity by optimizing site locations and targeting outreach to vulnerable populations. The Company’s business strategy focuses on reimagining the consumer healthcare experience to be more personalized, simpler, and increasingly digital, enabling care to be delivered when, where, and how consumers desire. It is shifting from transaction-based care to addressing holistic health—physical, emotional, social, and economic—to improve care quality and reduce medical costs. The Company is expanding into next-generation care delivery and health services to create new sources of value and improve satisfaction for both providers and consumers. The Company believes its consumer-centric approach will drive sustainable long-term growth and deliver value to all stakeholders. The report includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties, including those related to the impact of COVID-19, future revenue, operating income, earnings per share, sales trends, medical cost trends, membership, pharmacy benefits, retail and long-term care operations, investment spending, interest expense, tax rates, cash flow, debt, and strategic initiatives such as the proposed acquisition of Oak Street Health, Inc. and the pending acquisition of Signify Health, Inc. These statements are subject to significant risks and uncertainties and may differ materially from actual results. The Company has filed a report on and attestation to its management’s assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting under Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. The Company has not filed a report correcting previously issued financial statements or restating financials due to an error requiring a recovery analysis of incentive-based compensation for executive officers. The Company is a well-known seasoned issuer and has filed all required reports during the past 12 months and for the prior 90 days. It has submitted electronically all required Interactive Data Files and is classified as a large accelerated filer. The information in the definitive proxy statement for the 2023 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, to be filed within 120 days after the end of the fiscal year, is incorporated by reference into Parts III and IV of the report. References to competitors or other companies are illustrative and not indicative of exclusivity or proximity in competition.

The Health Care Benefits segment offers a range of commercial medical products, including point-of-service (POS), preferred provider organization (PPO), health maintenance organization (HMO), and indemnity benefit (Indemnity) plans, as well as health savings accounts (HSAs) and consumer-directed health plans that combine traditional POS or PPO and/or dental coverage with an accumulating benefit account, which may be funded by the plan sponsor and/or the member. With the launch of Aetna Virtual Primary Care™ in 2021, eligible members gain access to remote health services alongside in-person visits at MinuteClinic® locations. These products and services are primarily targeted at large multi-site national, mid-sized, and small employers, individual insureds, and expatriates. The Company provides medical stop loss insurance for employers who self-insure, assuming risk for large individual claims or aggregate losses above a pre-set annual threshold. Additional health products include dental plans, behavioral health, employee assistance programs, provider network access, and vision coverage. In select geographies, the segment offers Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, prescription drug coverage (PDP), Medicaid, and Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and participates in demonstration projects for individuals eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid (“Duals”). Medicare Advantage plans are offered through annual contracts with the U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) in 46 states and Washington, D.C. in 2022, with national Medicare PPO plans available for certain qualifying employer groups, forming an integrated national Insured Medicare product when combined with the Company’s PDP. The Company offers PDP plans in all 50 states and Washington, D.C. in 2022. Medicare Supplement products cover gaps in Original Medicare, including deductibles and coinsurance, and are available in 49 states and Washington, D.C. in 2022. Medicaid and CHIP services are provided in 16 states in 2022 on an Insured or ASC basis. For Duals, the Company coordinates 100% of care and may provide additional services to manage health care costs, with eligibility based on income and resource requirements. The Company maintains a nationwide provider network of approximately 1.6 million participating providers as of December 31, 2022, including physicians, hospitals, laboratories, imaging centers, and urgent care facilities. The Company seeks NCQA accreditation for its HMO and PPO plans, with Aetna Life Insurance Company (ALIC) receiving nationwide PPO Health Plan accreditation; as of December 31, 2022, all Commercial HMO and ALIC PPO members eligible for HMO or PPO plans were in NCQA-accredited plans. Provider selection and credentialing follow NCQA, URAC, state, and federal standards, and the Company is certified under the NCQA Credentials Verification Organization (CVO) program and holds URAC CVO accreditation. Quality assessment begins with initial verification of practitioner licenses, education, and work history, and requires hospitals to be CMS-certified or accredited by The Joint Commission, the American Osteopathic Association, or Det Norske Veritas Healthcare. The Company offers quality and outcome measurement, quality improvement, and health data analysis programs to providers and purchasers. The segment operates an end-to-end information technology suite supporting member engagement, enrollment, benefit administration, care management, operations, financial reporting, and analytics, with integration enabling real-time data transfer. Investments are focused on enterprise data platforms, cloud capabilities, digital products, and emerging technologies like voice, artificial intelligence, and robotics to automate processes, reduce costs, and improve member experience. Medical membership is distributed across the United States and certain international locations, with products marketed to employers, individuals, college students, part-time workers, health plans, government entities, labor groups, and expatriates. Commercial Insured and ASC products are primarily sold to employers, with employees selecting coverage during annual open enrollment; employers typically pay premiums and employees reimburse a portion via payroll deductions, while some plans are fully employee-funded. The Company bills individuals directly in certain cases. Effective January 2022, it entered individual public health insurance exchanges in eight states, expanding to four additional states in January 2023. Insured Medicare coverage is offered individually and through employer groups to retirees, Medicaid and CHIP members are enrolled individually, and Duals members receive Insured coverage. Products are sold through the Company’s sales personnel, independent brokers, agents, consultants, private health insurance exchanges, and public exchanges. Brokers may receive commissions, fees, or other payments, with the Company collecting funds from customers and remitting them to brokers. Marketing includes television, radio, billboards, print media, social media, market research, and direct marketing. The U.S. federal government is a significant customer through CMS contracts, accounting for 14% of consolidated revenues in 2022, 2021, and 2020, with CMS contracts for Medicare coverage representing approximately 74%, 79%, and 78% of federal government revenues in those years, respectively. Commercial Insured plan pricing is established in advance, typically for one year, with fixed premiums; unanticipated cost increases are not recoverable in the current period, though future rates may be influenced by prior experience. Premiums are subject to state regulatory approval where required. Medicare Advantage and PDP contracts with CMS involve fixed per-member (capitation) payments or portions of premiums, adjusted for demographics and health risk, with CMS considering inflation, utilization, and fee-for-service costs. PDP contracts include risk-sharing with CMS. Payments are subject to annual revision by CMS, and premiums are subject to federal audits, which may result in retroactive or prospective adjustments and refunds. Some Medicare Advantage and PDP plans require supplemental premiums, which may be adjusted based on income or asset levels. Compared to commercial products, Medicare contracts generate higher per-member-per-month revenues and higher benefit costs. The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act and the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act of 2010 (the “ACA”) tie a portion of Medicare Advantage reimbursement to star ratings, requiring at least a 4-star rating to qualify for bonus payments. CMS released the Company’s 2023 star ratings in October 2022; based on membership at December 31, 2022, 21% of Medicare Advantage members were in 4.0-star or higher plans in 2023, compared to 87% in 2022. Medicare Supplement rates are state-regulated and vary by state and plan. Under Insured Medicaid contracts, state agencies pay fixed monthly rates per member, which vary by state, line of business, and demographics, and are subject to change or adjustment for health risk; CMS requires actuarial soundness. ASC Medicaid contracts are typically for more than one year and may include performance incentives and limited financial risk sharing, with performance evaluated annually and risk share limited to a percentage of fees. Payments are subject to annual state appropriations. Duals contracts are established by CMS and state agencies, with potential for premium or refund adjustments if contractual or regulatory requirements are not met. The Company offers HMO and consumer-directed medical and dental plans to federal employees under the FEHB and Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Programs, with premium and fee rates subject to federal review and audit, which may result in retroactive or prospective adjustments and refunds. Beginning in 2014, the ACA imposed industry-wide fees, including the health insurer fee (HIF), which was repealed for calendar years after 2020. The Company aims to collect premiums or offset all ACA-related fees, assessments, and taxes. The segment’s quarterly operating income is affected by seasonal increases in benefit costs as members reach deductibles and out-of-pocket limits and by higher operating expenses in the fourth quarter due to plan year preparation and Medicare enrollment marketing. During the year ended December 31, 2022, the impact of COVID-19 stabilized as medical costs were captured in pricing, and the segment returned to normal seasonality. In 2021, the first quarter saw generally consistent medical costs but increased testing and treatment expenses and lower Medicare risk-adjusted revenue; testing and treatment costs declined in the second quarter and remained lower than in the first quarter; medical costs began to normalize in the third quarter.

The seasonality of benefit costs generally increases during the year as Insured members progress through their annual deductibles and out-of-pocket expense limits, while operating expenses are typically highest in the fourth quarter due to spending related to preparing for the upcoming plan year and Medicare annual enrollment marketing. During the year ended December 31, 2022, the impact of COVID-19 in the Health Care Benefits segment had generally stabilized as a result of the Company capturing COVID-19-related medical costs in pricing, leading to a return to a more normal seasonality pattern. In 2021, the customary quarterly operating income progression was disrupted by COVID-19; while first-quarter medical costs were generally consistent with historical baselines, the segment experienced increased testing and treatment costs and lower Medicare risk-adjusted revenue. In the second quarter, testing and treatment costs remained but at significantly lower levels than in the first quarter. Starting in the third quarter, medical costs rose due to the spread of emerging COVID-19 variants, driving increased testing and treatment costs that continued through the fourth quarter. In 2020, the customary quarterly operating income progression was also affected by COVID-19, with a significant reduction in discretionary utilization and cancellation of elective procedures beginning in mid-March, utilization remaining below historical levels through April, recovering in May and June, and reaching more normal levels in the third and fourth quarters, with some geographic areas impacted by subsequent COVID-19 waves. The health care benefits industry is highly competitive due to numerous for-profit and not-for-profit competitors, marketing and pricing strategies, and a wide range of competing products, including new introductions. New entrants and industry consolidation are expected to intensify competition, and the shift toward a consumer-focused retail marketplace, including Insurance Exchanges, and increased use of technology heighten risks from new entrants and disruptive actions by existing competitors. Key factors distinguishing health plans include perceived quality (including accreditation), service quality, coverage comprehensiveness, cost (premiums, provider discounts, out-of-pocket costs), product design, financial stability and ratings, provider network breadth and quality, availability of network options, provider access, and member support and care management. The Company believes it is competitive on all these factors, and its ability to grow membership or Health Care Benefits segment revenues depends on differentiating itself on these points. Competition may also affect provider availability, including primary care physicians, specialists, and hospitals. Insured products compete with local and regional health plans, other large commercial health care benefit insurers, health system-owned plans, new entrants, and numerous for-profit and not-for-profit organizations licensed by the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Association. The largest competitor in Medicare products is Original Medicare. Additional competitors include medical and dental provider organizations, specialty service providers (such as pharmacy benefit management providers), health care consultants, financial services firms, integrated health care delivery organizations, third-party administrators, HIT companies, and government-sponsored programs. Emerging competitors include startup health plans, technology companies, provider-owned plans, joint ventures (including not-for-profit ones), financial services firms distributing products on private exchanges, consulting firms distributing products on private exchanges, and non-traditional distributors like retail companies. The Company’s ability to grow enrollment in Insured Commercial Medical products is also influenced by employers’ willingness to self-fund health coverage. The Health Care Benefits segment’s ASC plans compete primarily with large commercial health care benefit companies, numerous for-profit and not-for-profit organizations under Blue Cross and Blue Shield licenses, and TPAs. The provider solutions and HIT markets are evolving rapidly, with competition coming from large health plans, commercial insurers, IT companies, and firms specializing in provider solutions and HIT. Many IT competitors have longer histories, stronger brand recognition, greater market presence, and more experience in developing innovative products. Competitive pressures affect the Company’s ability to acquire or retain customers, and medical membership may be negatively impacted by adverse economic conditions and workforce reductions among existing customers, particularly in the U.S. and concentrated industries. The Company has several reinsurance agreements with non-affiliated insurers for Health Care Benefits policies to reduce the risk of catastrophic losses and lower capital and surplus requirements, and regularly evaluates and refines its reinsurance and risk management strategies. The Pharmacy Services segment offers a full range of PBM solutions, including plan design, administration, formulary management, retail pharmacy network management, and mail order pharmacy services. It also provides specialty pharmacy and infusion services, clinical services, disease management, medical spend management, and administrative services for providers and federal 340B program covered entities. The Company operates a group purchasing organization that negotiates pharmaceutical pricing and rebates with manufacturers on behalf of participants and provides administrative and management services to manufacturers. Clients include employers, insurance companies, unions, government employee groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid plans, plans on Insurance Exchanges, and other health benefit sponsors. The segment operates retail specialty pharmacies, specialty mail order pharmacies, mail order dispensing pharmacies, compounding pharmacies, and infusion and enteral nutrition branches. During the year ended December 31, 2022, the Company’s PBM filled or managed 2.3 billion prescriptions on a 30-day equivalent basis. The Company dispenses prescriptions directly through mail order and retail pharmacies, with all prescriptions analyzed, processed, and documented using proprietary systems that automate reviews for plan eligibility, early refills, duplicate dispensing, drug interactions or allergies, over-utilization, and potential fraud. The Company assists clients in designing pharmacy benefit plans to improve health outcomes and reduce costs, using proprietary software and formal performance reviews, and recommends plans that promote lower-cost, clinically appropriate drugs, including generic equivalents, and allow clients to set different member payment levels for various drugs to encourage cost-effective choices. The Company uses the CVS Caremark National Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee, an independent panel of medical experts, to review and approve drugs for inclusion in its template formularies, ensuring safety, efficacy, and clinical appropriateness while helping drive the lowest net cost for clients. The formularies include recommended products across drug classes with alternatives available, and the Company conducts ongoing independent reviews of all drugs, including generics. Clients can adopt template formularies, and members receive real-time benefits information at the point of prescribing, at CVS pharmacies, and directly. The Company maintains a national network of approximately 66,000 retail pharmacies—about 40,000 chain pharmacies (including CVS locations) and 26,000 independent pharmacies—across the U.S., Puerto Rico, the District of Columbia, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. When a prescription is filled, the pharmacy sends data electronically to the Company, which interfaces with proprietary systems to verify member eligibility and perform drug utilization reviews for clinical appropriateness and safety, confirming payment. Mail order pharmacies receive prescriptions or refill requests, primarily for maintenance medications, which are reviewed by staff pharmacists with the help of proprietary systems, potentially involving prescriber communication and resulting in generic substitution, therapeutic interchange, or other actions to reduce cost or improve treatment. The Company’s mail order pharmacies are accredited by URAC. Specialty mail order pharmacies, retail specialty pharmacies, and infusion/enteral nutrition branches are operated in the U.S., with specialty mail order pharmacies accredited by URAC, The Joint Commission, and the Accreditation Commission for Health Care (ACHC), which includes accreditation by the Pharmacy Compounding Accreditation Board for compliance with the highest compounding standards. The Company offers clinical programs to manage pharmacy and health care costs, including utilization management, medication management, quality assurance, adherence, and counseling to address inappropriate medication use and non-adherence. To combat prescription opioid abuse, the Company uses a seven-day supply limit for new patients, daily dosage limits based on opioid strength, and requires immediate-release formulations before extended-release opioids. The Pharmacy Advisor® program provides face-to-face and telephone counseling to members with chronic conditions like diabetes and cardiovascular disease to identify care gaps, improve adherence, and manage health. Digital connectivity enhances visibility to lower-cost alternatives through analytics and data sharing to reduce drug costs. Disease management programs cover conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, and multiple sclerosis and are accredited by NCQA. The UM program for similar conditions is accredited by NCQA and URAC. The NovoLogix® online preauthorization tool identifies outliers in specialty drug dosages and costs to capture savings and ensure clinically appropriate use. The Company operates a group purchasing organization that negotiates drug pricing and rebates and provides administrative and reporting services to manufacturers. The Pharmacy Services segment’s claim adjudication platform centralizes data from mail order prescriptions, retail claims, and other solutions, with the Health Engagement Engine® and proprietary clinical algorithms connecting enterprise functions to support cost management and health improvement using cloud-native technologies. This technology enables actionable interventions in retail, mail, specialty pharmacies, and customer care, leveraging enterprise data and assisted artificial intelligence to deliver insights and automate manual tasks. Specialty services integrate with the claim adjudication platform and health plan adjudication systems through a centralized architecture serving many clients and members. Operating services such as Specialty Expedite® provide an interconnected onboarding solution for specialty medications and total patient management branding, managed through an innovative specialty workflow and web platform. Pharmacy Services clients include employers, insurance companies, unions, government employee groups, health plans, PDPs, Managed Medicaid plans, plans on Insurance Exchanges, and other health benefit sponsors. Pharmaceuticals are provided to eligible members in client benefit plans using the Company’s information systems for safety checks, drug interaction screening, and generic substitution opportunities. Substantially all Pharmacy Services segment revenues come from dispensing and managing prescription drugs for eligible members in client benefit plans. Pharmacy Services segment revenues are not seasonal. The primary competitive factors in the pharmacy services industry include the ability to negotiate favorable discounts from drug manufacturers and access to retail pharmacy networks, effective cost management using clinical strategies and preferred formularies, marketing of PBM products, commitment to flexible, clinically-oriented services, quality, scope, and cost of services, and operational excellence. The segment faces significant competition from large national PBMs (e.g., Prime Therapeutics, MedImpact), PBMs owned by major health plans (e.g., Express Scripts of Cigna, OptumRx of UnitedHealth), and smaller standalone PBMs. The Retail/LTC segment sells prescription drugs and health and wellness products, provides health care services through MinuteClinic walk-in clinics, offers medical diagnostic testing, administers vaccinations for influenza, COVID-19, and shingles, and conducts long-term care pharmacy operations, distributing prescription drugs and providing pharmacy consulting and ancillary services to long-term care facilities. As of December 31, 2022, the Retail/LTC segment operated more than 9,000 retail locations, over 1,100 MinuteClinic locations, and online retail pharmacy websites, LTC pharmacies, and on-site pharmacies. During the year ended December 31, 2022, the Retail/LTC segment filled 1.6 billion prescriptions on a 30-day equivalent basis, and the Company dispensed approximately 26.8% of total U.S. retail pharmacy prescriptions. A typical retail store sells prescription drugs and a wide range of nationally advertised brand and proprietary merchandise, with pharmacy locations sometimes contracting with Covered Entities under the 340B program. Front store categories include over-the-counter drugs, consumer health products, beauty, and personal care items. The Company sources products from numerous manufacturers and distributors, believing competitive sources are readily available for most products, and the loss of any single supplier would not materially affect the segment. LTC operations include prescription drug distribution and related consulting and ancillary services. MinuteClinic locations offer a variety of health care services. Retail/LTC revenues by major product group are as follows: Pharmacy (1) accounted for 76.9% of revenues in 2022.

For the year ended December 31, 2022, the Company dispensed approximately 26.8% of the total retail pharmacy prescriptions in the United States, with 1.6 billion prescriptions on a 30-day equivalent basis. The Retail/LTC segment includes retail pharmacy operations and long-term care (LTC) services, where pharmacy revenues accounted for 76.9% of segment revenues in 2022, 2021, and 2020, with front store and other revenues making up the remaining 23.1%. Pharmacy revenues are driven by industry trends such as an aging population, increased prescription drug use, new pharmaceuticals, vaccination needs including the COVID-19 vaccine, and Medicare Part D growth. The Company offers integrated pharmacy health care services to support medication management and improve health outcomes. Front store revenues are supported by innovative product offerings, including the ExtraCare® loyalty program and CarePass® membership, and the Company carries approximately 5,500 proprietary brand products, which represented about 21% of front store revenues in 2022. As of December 31, 2022, the Company operated more than 1,100 MinuteClinic locations, staffed by nurse practitioners and physician assistants, providing convenient, cost-effective care and offering virtual care services. MinuteClinic collaborates with Health Care Benefits and Pharmacy Services segments to improve member health and reduce costs and maintains relationships with leading hospitals and physicians. The Company also operates on-site pharmacies at client sites for prescription filling and vaccinations, including the COVID-19 vaccine. Medical diagnostic testing is available through CVS pharmacy locations, MinuteClinic, community-based sites, and the Return Ready solution. LTC pharmacy services are provided through Omnicare®, serving skilled nursing facilities, assisted living communities, hospitals, correctional facilities, and other health care providers, with services including monthly drug therapy evaluations and pharmaceutical case management for retirees, employees, and dependents. During 2022, the Company opened approximately 40 new locations, relocated 4, and closed about 300 locations, as part of a strategic review that began in the fourth quarter of 2021 and included plans to close approximately 900 retail stores between 2022 and 2024. The Company continues to invest in information systems, including the WeCARE Workflow tool, Health Engagement Engine, and Omniview® digital technology suite, which support pharmacy operations, patient care, and digital access to services such as appointment scheduling, test and vaccine administration, and digital recordkeeping. Retail/LTC segment revenues are not seasonally impacted, except for front store revenues, which peak during the December holiday season, and both pharmacy and front store revenues are affected by the cough, cold, and flu season and extreme weather. During 2022, the first quarter saw high volumes of COVID-19 vaccinations and OTC test kit sales, with the highest quarterly volume of diagnostic tests; second and third quarters saw continued earnings from OTC test kits and lower levels of diagnostic testing and vaccinations; the fourth quarter saw increased vaccine administration due to the bivalent booster. In 2021 and 2020, the segment’s performance was also impacted by the pandemic, with reduced customer traffic in 2021 due to a weaker flu season and reduced traffic in 2020 due to shelter-in-place orders and decreased prescriptions. The retail pharmacy business is highly competitive, with the Company competing on store location, customer service, product selection, and price, facing competition from drugstore chains like Walgreens and Rite Aid, supermarkets, discount retailers like Walmart, independent pharmacies, internet companies like Amazon, and other health care providers. LTC pharmacy services are highly regional and competitive, with PharMerica being the Company’s largest national competitor, and some states imposing “freedom of choice” laws that increase competition in Medicaid programs. The Corporate/Other segment includes management and administrative expenses and products no longer accepted by new customers, such as large case pensions and long-term care insurance. The Company and Cardinal Health each own 50% of Red Oak Sourcing, LLC, a generic pharmaceutical sourcing entity that sources and negotiates supply contracts without holding inventory. The Company funds growth through cash flow, commercial paper, short-term and long-term borrowings. Most employer groups, individuals, college students, part-time workers, health plans, providers, governmental units, labor groups, and expatriates settle payments within less than 30 days, while Medicare Part D services settle with CMS over several quarters. Most non-pharmacy revenues are paid in cash or via debit/credit cards, and most pharmacy revenues are settled within less than 30 days. As of December 31, 2022, the Company employed over 300,000 colleagues, primarily in the United States, including all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico, with approximately 73% being full-time. The Company conducts annual internal engagement surveys, with over 80% of colleagues participating in 2022 and over 75% reporting active engagement. The Board, CEO, and Chief People Officer oversee human capital strategy in total rewards, diversity, equity and inclusion, colleague development, and health and safety. Total rewards include competitive wages, annual bonuses, 401(k) plans, stock awards, health benefits, paid time off, flexible schedules, family leave, dependent care resources, tuition assistance, and colleague assistance programs. In 2021, the Company increased its minimum hourly wage to $15.00 effective July 2022, with incremental increases to competitive hourly rates beginning in August 2021.
